leftEvidence.role: Silence and Elijah on the descent
leftEvidence.title: Jesus commands silence until resurrection and speaks of Elijah

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: As they descend, Jesus tells the disciples not to report the vision until the Son of Man rises from the dead.
points.right: On the descent Jesus commands silence until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Their Elijah question leads Jesus to speak of Elijah’s coming, rejection, and the Son of Man’s suffering; they understand him to mean John the Baptizer.
points.right: The three keep the saying while questioning what rising means, then ask about Elijah and hear of suffering already done to him.

payload.posture: Matthew and Mark preserve the silence command, resurrection boundary, and Elijah question.

rightEvidence.role: Silence and Elijah on the descent
rightEvidence.title: The three keep the event to themselves and question rising

payload.tension: Mark foregrounds questioning about rising; Matthew names the disciples’ conclusion about John the Baptizer.
payload.title: Two accounts of the descent
